extraction.name: OpenBookQA
extraction.description: A new kind of question answering dataset modeled after open book exams for assessing human understanding of a subject. It consists of roughly 6000 multiple-choice questions that probe an understanding of 1326 elementary level science facts and their application to novel situations, requiring combining an open book fact with broad common knowledge.
extraction.creator: Todor Mihaylov, Peter Clark, Tushar Khot, Ashish Sabharwal
extraction.citeAs: Mihaylov, T., Clark, P., Khot, T., & Sabharwal, A. (2018). Can a Suit of Armor Conduct Electricity? A New Dataset for Open Book Question Answering. arXiv:1809.02789.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: A multi-stage process starting with a set of core science facts (F), using crowd-sourcing to generate questions based on F that probe novel situations, using an automatic filter to ensure hardness for retrieval and association based systems, using a crowd filter to ensure answerability by a lay person, and further using an expert filter to ensure higher quality in Dev and Test sets.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: The crowdsourced second facts (k) were often incomplete, over-complete, or only distantly related to the question.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: A subset of the WorldTree corpus (1326 facts marked as 'central') and broad common knowledge expected from sources like ConceptNet, Wikipedia, or a corpus with 14M science-related sentences.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The answer choices of questions were randomly shuffled to avoid unintended bias. Dev and Test splits were further filtered by an in-house expert.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Verification of basic checks: exactly 4 answer choices; no negation words; uniform answer choice length. Questions were fed to an information retrieval solver and a word association based solver to verify that neither answered correctly and top 3 IR retrieved sentences were insufficient; if not, the question was edited and re-tried.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Crowd-workers were shown a random science fact, asked to think of a second common fact to combine with it, convert the derived assertion into a question-answer pair, and add 3 incorrect answer choices. 5 new crowd-workers then answered the question; it was kept only if at least 4 answered correctly.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Questions were deemed answerable if at least 4 out of 5 workers answered correctly. Analysis showed Choice 'A' was the correct answer in 69% of questions before shuffling. Human performance was estimated at ~92%.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Workers from North America with a 'masters' level qualification.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Information retrieval solver (Clark et al., 2016) and a word association based solver (Turney, 2017)
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Inevitable human bias in crowdsourced datasets (e.g., plausible answer detector achieved 49.6% accuracy). Workers generally start with the correct answer and create homogeneous incorrect ones (odd-one-out solver achieved 50.2%). Choice 'A' was correct 69% of the time before shuffling.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The additional facts (k) provided are noisy (incomplete, over-complete, or distantly related). In 21% of cases, the crowdsourced question tests a fact that doesn't necessarily need the original science fact. The dataset requires multi-hop reasoning with partial context, making it challenging for current models.
